subject: SLO probing & warm-up playbook — post-demo action items
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Zhang <elliot.z@fastpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-02T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: SLO probing & warm-up playbook — post-demo action items

Elliot,

Thanks for the call earlier — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for verifying SLOs and burst behavior.

Key SLOs discussed (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 <= 100 ms for short completions (<= 32 tokens); p99 <= 250 ms for streaming sessions (per-token delivery)
- Throughput: steady-state 150 QPS across auth region; peak burst concurrency target 600-1,000 sessions
- Streaming: token-level streaming with tail latency under 200 ms for first token after model emits

Autoscaling primitives we propose to validate:
- Warm pool: target 30 pre-warmed instances in us-west-2 for first pass (we recommend 30-50 depending on observed session mix)
- Scale-up targets: warm-pool activation < 15s; cold provisioning fallback < 90s
- Queueing behavior: bounded queue with soft-failover to lower-cost quantized model after 10s queue wait

Immediate validation plan (asks):
1) You'll share a 24-hour traffic sample (RPS by minute, session length distribution) — place in the Drive link below by EOD Tue 2028-05-07
2) We will run two tests next week: a 30-minute spike to 2x peak, and a 1-hour soak at target peak to measure tail behavior
3) We'll instrument token-level latencies, KV-cache hit rates, and request trace IDs for every test

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (proposal), latency-heatmap.png (demo snapshot)

If the SLO numbers above look off, call them out. Otherwise we'll schedule the validation window and deliver a short runbook for the test.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
From: Elliot Zhang <elliot.z@fastpay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: FastPay SRE Team <sre@fastpay.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO probing & warm-up playbook — post-demo action items

Monica,

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming numbers with a few clarifications from our side:
- Workload mix: ~65% short completions (avg 40 tokens), ~35% long streaming sessions (avg 800 tokens emitted over time)
- Typical burst profile: baseline ~120 QPS, short spikes to ~900 concurrent sessions for up to 10 minutes during end-of-month batch processes
- Peak token emission rate during spikes can reach ~120k tokens/minute

We will upload the 24-hour sample to the Drive link you provided by Monday 2028-05-07. Also cc'ing the SRE channel so they can confirm encryption and network constraints for tests.

One ask: during the spike test please avoid routing live traffic to any canary models — we need the test to be fully isolated (can you run in dedicated test pool or labeled tenant?)

On another note, we have a compliance question about retention of token-level logs for 30 days. I'll send that separately to your security contact.

Thanks,
Elliot
Elliot Zhang
SRE Manager, FastPay
elliot.z@fastpay.com

Date: 2028-05-04T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO probing & warm-up playbook — technical validation notes

Elliot,

Thanks — I pulled the demo traces and sketched a validation plan with runbook details below.

Notes and assumptions
- Streaming semantics: we will validate per-token latency using a synthetic harness that mirrors your avg session emission profile (we'll parameterize by tokens/sec)
- Cache behavior: recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for short completions to meet p95 targets; if cache hit-rate < 70% we'll expect 15-25% latency regression at p95

Warm pool and scale timelines (estimates based on our runtime):
- Warm-pool instance activation: 8-12s from activation signal to accepting first request (includes container ready + model loaded in memory)
- Cold provision: 45-90s (GPU allocation + model load) — plan tests to rely on warm pool for spike response
- Priming sequence: run 3 short warmup requests per instance (32 tokens) to populate KV cache and trigger JIT paths

Queueing and graceful degradation
- We recommend a bounded async queue per-tenant with 10s target wait window; after 10s we will route to a quantized model variant with configured quality guardrails
- Backlog limit: configurable; propose 5k tokens total across queue before rejecting new sessions

Validation tests we propose
1) Spike test: 15 minutes at 2x peak concurrent sessions, measure p95/p99 per-token latency and tail token drop
2) Soak test: 60 minutes at sustained peak to watch queueing and cache warmup dynamics
3) Priming verification: run repeated warmup sequences across warm pool instances and collect KV hit-rate

I'll attach a sample warmup log to illustrate expected metrics and include a short script for the token-level harness. We can run the spike test in a labeled dedicated test pool so it doesn't touch canary or prod tenants.

If all good, propose we lock the May 10 window for the spike and May 11 for the soak. Monica — can you confirm scheduling and whether FastPay needs a signed test addendum?

Thanks,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
